timeline.name: A Brief History of Fogport
timeline.entry: Fogport dates its recent history from the wound that divided the city into Before and After. Earlier dates are approximate; the catastrophe destroyed three royal archives and caused a fourth to insist that it had not yet been written.

entities.name: House Heliot
entities.entry:
House Heliot ruled Fogport from the raising of its first sea wall until the Catastrophe. The dynasty favored magnificent public works, heroic statues, very long building names, and the placement of royal monograms upon objects which plainly did not require them.

The Old Palace and nearly the entire royal household vanished during the Catastrophe. The Crown has never been legally abolished. It is officially in abeyance for the duration of the emergency, a phrase now forty-three years old.

posts.name: GAMEMASTER SECRETS — House Heliot
posts.entry:
• Queen Adelaine IV authorized the Continuance Engine after being convinced that Fogport faced eventual destruction.
  • The royal household was inside the Old Palace when the buried civic complex collapsed.
  • No complete list of survivors exists. A legitimate claimant may still live, but none has yet been established.

entities.name: Lord Protector Silas Crake
entities.entry:
Silas Crake has governed Fogport under emergency authority for forty-two years. Each year, at precisely 11:17 on the anniversary of the Catastrophe, he renews the Continuance Emergency for one further year.

He does not wear a crown. He does not sit upon the Empty Throne. He does not permit anyone to call him king. His narrow, black-clad portrait nevertheless hangs in schools, tram stations, ministry halls, police offices, and every shop licensed to sell more than six eels at once.

Crake speaks softly, signs everything in green ink, and ends every proclamation with the same promise: Until the City Is Safe. Fogporters commonly say the emergency will end next Thursday. No one specifies which Thursday.

posts.name: GAMEMASTER SECRETS — Silas Crake
posts.entry:
• Crake was Deputy Comptroller of Royal Works when the Catastrophe occurred. He seized the ration depots, government presses, tram guards, and surviving ministries before anyone else understood that House Heliot was gone.
  • He did not design the Continuance Engine, but he helped conceal its purpose and knows that the wards of Fogport paid part of its price.
  • He fears a legitimate Heliot claimant more than a popular uprising: a claimant could end his emergency authority with a signature.
  • Crake knows the machinery beneath the Old Palace is not entirely dead.

entities.name: The First Sea Wall and Royal Charter
entities.entry: House Heliot raised the first stone sea wall around the deep harbor and declared the crowded settlement behind it the Royal City of Fogport. The harbor promptly flooded through an unfinished ceremonial gate, but the charter had already been printed and was therefore considered binding.

entities.name: The Blackwake Civic Quarter Opens
entities.entry: The Crown opened Fogport's first purpose-built ministry quarter at Blackwake: courts, records halls, pumping houses, public baths, and seventeen offices responsible for regulating one another. Citizens were promised that every civic problem would now have a proper window at which to queue.

entities.name: Grand Heliot Station Opens
entities.entry: Grand Heliot Station opened beneath a glass-and-iron roof, binding Fogport's districts to its docks and to the cities beyond the Sayir Sea. The first royal tram arrived eleven minutes late, carrying two conductors, a brass band, and one passenger whom nobody remembered inviting.

entities.name: The Great Continuance Works Announced
entities.entry:
Queen Adelaine IV announced the Great Continuance Works, a generation-long program of reinforced bridges, modern pumping stations, expanded tramways, new monuments, and improvements beneath the Old Palace. Its slogan appeared on banners, bonds, school copybooks, and commemorative spoons:

FOGPORT SHALL ENDURE.

posts.name: GAMEMASTER SECRETS — The Great Continuance Works
posts.entry: The visible public works secretly connected tram rails, bridges, waterways, monuments, ministries, and the Old Palace into one city-sized magical Operation: the Continuance Engine.

entities.name: The Catastrophe
entities.entry:
At 11:17 in the morning, every bell in Fogport rang once. No hand touched a rope.

Tram rails flashed white. The harbor climbed the sea walls. The Old Palace sank with most of House Heliot, and whole districts folded, slid, or simply ceased to continue. Streets ended in open air. Houses stood sliced through, their rooms exposed to the rain. Thousands vanished without leaving bodies.

The children registered in the royal orphanages survived. They came out changed: black-eyed, clawed, terribly strong—and no longer capable of growing older. Fogport would come to call them the Gutterkin.

The official inquiry blamed an unforeseeable failure within the Great Continuance Works. Its findings filled twelve locked volumes. Forty-three years later, the repairs continue, the emergency remains in force, and many public clocks omit the minute 11:17 entirely.

Fogport endured.

posts.name: GAMEMASTER SECRETS — The Catastrophe
posts.entry:
Beneath the Old Palace, royal magicians, civic engineers, and industrial contractors built the Continuance Engine. Fogport's tram rails, bridges, monuments, waterways, and public buildings formed one city-sized magical Operation with a single command: Fogport shall endure.

The Operation succeeded. Magic could not preserve the city without taking continuance from somewhere else, so the Engine stole futures from Fogport's people, buildings, streets, and districts. Some places collapsed. Others were displaced. Thousands had every unwritten tomorrow taken from them at once.

The royal orphans were legally registered as wards of Fogport. In the merciless grammar of the Operation, they belonged to the city more completely than anyone else. Their futures were taken first. They cannot age. Their missing adulthood remains compressed inside their small bodies, giving them monstrous strength; the blackening at their hands and feet marks the edge of that theft.

The Engine is ruined, buried, and not entirely inactive. Its vast civic complex beneath the former palace is Fogport's great dungeon and the deepest surviving wound of the Catastrophe.

entities.name: The Emergency Protectorate Is Declared
entities.entry:
With the Crown missing, ministries quarreling, and portions of Fogport still burning underwater, Deputy Comptroller Silas Crake assumed emergency control of the ration depots, tram guards, and government presses. Parliament granted him the title Lord Protector for ninety days.

The ninety days have so far lasted forty-two years.

entities.name: Gutterkin
entities.entry:
Every city has abandoned children. Fogport has children who abandoned civilization.

The Gutterkin look, at first, like ordinary children: small bodies, young faces, and tangled, wind-wild hair. A closer look reveals their shark-black eyes, sharp teeth, and clawed hands and feet. Their skin darkens along the fingers and toes until the tips are pure black. They sometimes steal clothing, but what they wear is usually ragged, mismatched, and scavenged from people who no longer need it.

They may look like children, but they are far stronger than grown adults. Even the strongest sailor would be wise not to grapple with one. Monsters and men alike fear them—and both have reason.

Gutterkin live in rooftops, sewers, abandoned factories, collapsed districts, and other spaces the city believes empty. They know Fogport's forgotten ways better than almost anyone. They can appear without a sound and vanish just as quickly.

Not all Gutterkin are alike. Some are playful, mischievous, or merely hungry. Many steal. Some beg. A few will guide travellers for food, treasure, or a favor. Others hunt in packs, kill without hesitation, and eat human flesh.

They were ordinary children once: wards of Fogport's royal orphanages who survived the Catastrophe changed. Forty-three years later, they still have not grown a day older. Certain tunnels beneath Nine Spoons now belong to them so completely that even the Feratu will not enter.

Never underestimate the children of Fogport. Especially when there are too many of them. Especially when they are smiling.

posts.name: GAMEMASTER SECRETS — Gutterkin
posts.entry:
• The Gutterkin were ordinary children registered as wards of Fogport when the Continuance Engine took their futures.
  • They are truly ageless. Their missing adulthood is compressed inside their small bodies and expresses itself as monstrous strength.
  • The blackening of their fingers and toes is the visible boundary of the theft.
  • Different Gutterkin bands may be playful, transactional, protective, predatory, or cannibalistic. They do not share one temperament or allegiance.
  • Nettle is Gutterkin, but her history, loyalties, and relationship to any particular band remain unresolved.

entities.name: Saint Orra of the Last Light
entities.type: Patron Saint of Those Finding Their Way Home
entities.entry:
Saint Orra predates House Heliot. During the Black Founding Storm, she climbed the old chapel tower and burned its pews, books, doors, and roof to keep one harbor light alive for three nights. More than a hundred boats followed it home. At dawn she was gone; scorched footprints went up the tower, but none came down.

She is patron of sailors, lamplighters, tram conductors, missing children, and anyone trying to find the way home. Fogporters insist: Orra belongs to the city, not the Crown.

posts.name: GAMEMASTER SECRETS — Saint Orra
posts.entry: Orra's beacon magically took the idea of being lost from the sailors below. The price may have been Orra's own place in the world. No grave, birth record, or reliable portrait of her exists.

entities.name: Captain Mirelle Vane
entities.entry:
Mirelle Vane was a tugmaster, salvager, union negotiator, and Fogport's favorite harbor hero. During the Black Gale she lit the drowned channels with a chain of burning boats and brought thirty-one vessels home.

Official portraits give her a naval coat she never owned. Dockside versions show her correctly: sleeves rolled, nose broken, one boot full of seawater, and smoking beneath a NO SMOKING notice.

entities.name: Sister Ilyra Fenn
entities.entry:
Ilyra Fenn was seven when the Catastrophe took her parents. She became a street physician, treating anyone who reached her door before asking whether they could pay.

During the War of Shut Gates, Fenn opened South Gate and brought food into the sealed districts. Her red shawl hangs above Hushwater Hospital.

posts.name: GAMEMASTER SECRETS — Sister Ilyra Fenn
posts.entry: Fenn's ledgers prove the Protectorate exaggerated the postwar fever and knowingly withheld food and medicine from the southern districts.

entities.name: The Last Light
entities.entry:
During the Black Founding Storm, the nameless priestess of the lighthouse chapel kept one beacon burning for three nights and guided more than a hundred boats home. The church later named her Saint Orra, the first saint of the goddess Orra.

The storm brought Fogport’s first green fog, which never left. The old town of Fogfort eventually became Fogport.

entities.name: The Three-Hour War
entities.entry: A royal cutter tried to seize the Harbor Guild's floating counting-house. The Guild chained the harbor and fired ceremonial cannon loaded with invoices. Three hours later the Crown withdrew and both sides declared victory. Fogport still uses Three-Hour War for any short, unnecessary quarrel.

posts.name: GAMEMASTER SECRETS — The Three-Hour War
posts.entry: The counting-house held ledgers proving House Heliot had imported forbidden magical apparatus. The surviving books were transferred beneath the Old Palace.

entities.name: Mirelle Vane Is Born
entities.entry: Mirelle Vane was born aboard the salvage tug Indelicate during a collision. Her birth certificate lists her birthplace as Dock 14, the Sayir Sea, and "under protest."

entities.name: The Royal Menagerie Opens
entities.entry: The Royal Menagerie opened beneath Crown Hill with iron galleries, flooded vaults, and creatures acquired through diplomacy, purchase, confiscation, and clerical error. Its lower exhibits were sealed after the Catastrophe and never fully inventoried.

posts.name: GAMEMASTER SECRETS — The Royal Menagerie
posts.entry: The deepest galleries collapsed into the buried Continuance complex. Several enclosures remain intact and their feeding mechanisms still operate. The Menagerie is an upper approach to Fogport's great dungeon.

entities.name: The Night of Ten Thousand Lanterns
entities.entry: During the Black Gale, Captain Mirelle Vane set every available boat alight and anchored them through the drowned channel. Thirty-one ships followed the burning road home; the thirty-second arrived next morning carrying only wet footprints.

entities.name: The Raising of Saint Orra
entities.entry: House Heliot raised the colossal statue of Saint Orra over a circular tram plaza, her caged lamp held above the rooftops. Grand Heliot Station was built around her in a radial plan, making the people's saint the unwilling centerpiece of royal modernity.

entities.name: Captain Mirelle Vane Dies
entities.entry: Mirelle Vane died at seventy-four steering a runaway funeral barge away from a school ferry. She asked to be buried facing the harbor so she could "keep an eye on the bastards." Dockworkers turn her statue seaward every year; the Ministry turns it back.

entities.name: Ilyra Fenn Is Born
entities.entry: Ilyra Fenn was born above a Nine Spoons washhouse during a storm that rained tiny clear frogs. Her mother kept three in a jam jar; one survived longer than anyone expected.

entities.name: The Seven-Day Bread Riot
entities.entry: When ration officers reserved Blackwake's flour for ministries and soldiers, bakers opened their ovens to the public. Citizens defended the bread lines with peel boards, soup ladles, roof tiles, and one extremely patient donkey. Fogport bakers have considered themselves a branch of government ever since.

entities.name: The War of Shut Gates
entities.entry: A foreign quarantine fleet blockaded Fogport after ships arrived with impossible cargo and passengers who cast no reflections. Lord Protector Crake sealed the landward gates too, trapping the poorest districts between hunger and the guns offshore. The siege ended after Sister Ilyra Fenn opened South Gate.

posts.name: GAMEMASTER SECRETS — The War of Shut Gates
posts.entry: Crake prolonged the closure for eleven months after the fleet offered terms. The sealed districts contained Continuance witnesses and an archivist who claimed Queen Adelaine had a living heir.

entities.name: Sister Fenn Opens South Gate
entities.entry: Ilyra Fenn crossed the barricades beneath a red hospital flag and persuaded the exhausted garrison to open South Gate. Her convoy brought flour, lamp oil, quinine, and forty-seven letters the Ministry had refused to deliver.

entities.name: The Red Funeral of Ilyra Fenn
entities.entry: Ilyra Fenn died of lung fever contracted while treating prisoners. Mourners tied red cloth to every door between Nine Spoons and Blackwake. So many attended that her coffin reached the cemetery three days late with four passengers sitting on it.

entities.name: Hushwater Hospital Opens
entities.entry: Hushwater Hospital opened in a converted tram depot using money collected after Ilyra Fenn's funeral. It accepts the sick, poor, monstrous, and—between midnight and dawn—patients who are legally dead but remain capable of filling out forms. Its red doors never close.

entities.name: The Statues Turn Inward
entities.entry: During a windless night, seventy-three statues turned to face the vanished Old Palace. Saint Orra's enormous head bowed and her lamp burned black until dawn. The government blamed subsidence. None has permitted itself to be moved back.

posts.name: GAMEMASTER SECRETS — The Statues Turn Inward
posts.entry: The monuments were components in the Continuance Engine's city-sized diagram. Their movement shows the buried mechanism attempted to realign itself and has begun drawing a minute amount of continuance from the repaired city.

entities.name: The Isle Is Discovered
entities.entry: Sailors discover a small, rocky isle surrounded by dangerous currents. The island is later associated with the goddess Orra, patron of safe passage and returning travelers.

entities.name: The First Chapel Is Founded
entities.entry: A small lighthouse chapel dedicated to the goddess Orra is built on the isle’s highest crag. It serves as beacon, shrine, watchtower, and refuge for passing ships.

entities.name: The Chapel Settlement
entities.entry: Lighthouse keepers, fishermen, rope-makers, and their families establish a permanent settlement around the chapel. The isle is no longer merely a place ships visit; people now call it home.

entities.name: Fogfort Is Established
entities.entry: Defensive walls, storehouses, docks, and a harbor chain are constructed around the chapel settlement. The fortified harbor becomes known as Fogfort.

entities.name: House Heliot Establishes Itself
entities.entry: House Heliot becomes influential by financing harbor defenses, warehouses, and trade infrastructure. The family begins as patrons and administrators rather than monarchs.

entities.name: The Heliot Crown Is Established
entities.entry: House Heliot formally establishes a hereditary royal court over Fogfort. The court claims authority over the harbor, though the Church of Orra continues to insist that the city’s oldest sacred traditions belong to the people.

entities.name: The Century of Iron Piers
entities.entry: Despite its persistent local fog, Fogfort flourishes as a trade hub. Over roughly a century, the settlement expands beyond the rocky isle onto enormous iron piers, creating new docks, warehouses, workshops, and neighborhoods above the sea.

entities.name: The War of the 99 Kingdoms
entities.entry: The War of the 99 Kingdoms is a modern conflict among the surrounding kingdoms. Fogport is centrally located but was never part of the war. Its neutrality, ports, manufacturing, and access to trade make it indispensable to every side—and trusted by none.

elements.name: The Last Light
elements.entry: Orra keeps one light burning through the Black Founding Storm.
